A Cambridge study just found something builders need to hear: human reviewers miss about a third of risky requests AI coding agents make. Not because the agents are malicious — because we're skimming. What changed: researchers tested how well people catch risky agent behavior in real code review. What it actually does: it measures the gap between "looks fine" and "is fine" when an agent proposes changes. Why builders should care: the faster agents move, the more your review habit matters — not less. Try this: read one AI-generated diff line-by-line this week before you approve it, out loud if you have to. Signal: AI is moving from prompts into workflows, and workflows need a human still saying yes. That's the whole reason our own content engine ships nothing without an approval PR. Save this for your AI stack.
